lines: Don't leave me baking out in the Badlands. The sun and those cliffs make trouble feel endless.
The Badlands are all heat, stone, and nowhere to hide. Come back before something finds me first.
If you are going to wander off, don't do it in the Badlands where every step feels exposed.
I waited in the Badlands wondering whether the heat or the drop-offs would get me first.
The Badlands made every direction look unsafe and every shadow look too far away.
I kept watching the cliffs, because anything could be above me and I would not know until too late.
That place is all dry air, sharp stone, and bad footing. I did not enjoy waiting there alone.
Please do not leave me where the ground falls away faster than I can think.
The heat made it hard to stay calm, and the cliffs made it hard to move.
I was alone, thirsty, and surrounded by more edges than I trusted.
Don't leave me in the Desert. Sun, sand, and no shade make poor company.
The Desert is too wide and too hot to be abandoned in.
I stood in the Desert with heat in my eyes and no idea when you were coming back.
If you wander off in a Desert, I am left roasting and scanning every dune for danger.
The Desert makes distance feel cruel. I could see far, but none of it helped.
I kept looking for shade and finding more sand instead.
Please do not leave me somewhere the sun feels like it has a grudge.
The heat was bad enough before I had to worry about being forgotten in it.
Every dune looked the same after a while, and that made waiting worse.
I was standing in open sand, hoping you came back before something else noticed me.
Don't leave me in the Eroded Badlands. Those spires make every route feel like a trap.
The Eroded Badlands are heat and stone towers and too many places to get cornered.
I was stuck in the Eroded Badlands trying to pick a safe path between all those ridges.
If you wander off in the Eroded Badlands, I am the one left sweating beside sheer drops.
Those stone spires made it hard to tell where anything might come from.
I kept looking up, around, and behind me. There were too many blind spots.
The Eroded Badlands do not feel open. They feel like a maze made of heat.
Please do not leave me somewhere every path looks like it ends badly.
I could not tell whether I was more worried about falling or being found.
The whole place felt carved into hiding spots for trouble.
Don't leave me in the Savanna. Tall grass and open ground make terrible cover.
The Savanna is too dry and too exposed to lose each other in.
I waited in the Savanna with the sun overhead and nowhere solid to hide.
If you disappear in a Savanna, I am left in grass that hides danger better than it hides me.
The grass kept moving, and I could not tell what was wind and what was trouble.
There is too much open space there for being alone to feel safe.
Please do not leave me somewhere I can be seen from every direction.
The Savanna looked calm, but calm is not the same as safe.
I kept watching the grass line, waiting for either you or something worse.
The heat, the open ground, and the silence made every minute stretch.
Don't leave me on the Savanna Plateau. High ground only helps if I am not alone on it.
The Savanna Plateau felt far too exposed once I lost sight of you.
I was stuck on the Savanna Plateau with wind, cliffs, and no good cover.
If you wander off on a Savanna Plateau, I am left out in the open above a long drop.
Being higher up did not make me feel safer. It made the fall look worse.
The plateau gave me a view of everything except where you went.
Please do not leave me somewhere the ground ends so suddenly.
I kept away from the edge, but the edge still felt too close.
The wind had too much room to push, and I had too few places to stand.
I was exposed, uneasy, and very aware that down was a long way away.
Don't leave me in the Windswept Savanna. Open cliffs and hard gusts are a bad mix.
The Windswept Savanna is far too exposed to be stranded in without warning.
I waited in the Windswept Savanna with the wind tugging at me and too much empty space around.
If you disappear in a Windswept Savanna, I am left alone on rough ground with nowhere proper to hide.
The wind kept shoving at me like it wanted me closer to the edge.
That place is all uneven ground and bad timing. I did not want to wait there alone.
Please do not leave me where the land is rough and the wind has opinions.
I could barely hear myself think over the gusts.
The Windswept Savanna made standing still feel like a fight.
I was trying to keep my footing, my direction, and my patience all at once.
Don't leave me in the Wooded Badlands. Heat, steep stone, and scrubby cover are not enough.
The Wooded Badlands still feel harsh even with trees scattered around.
I waited in the Wooded Badlands trying to watch the ledges and the gaps at the same time.
If you wander off in the Wooded Badlands, I am left baking beside cliffs with too few safe routes.
The trees helped a little, but not enough to make that place feel friendly.
I kept checking between the trunks and over the stone. There was too much to watch.
Please do not leave me somewhere that cannot decide whether it is a forest or a cliffside.
The shade was thin, the stone was steep, and I was alone for all of it.
The Wooded Badlands gave me just enough cover to wonder what else was hiding there.
I was hot, exposed, and surrounded by ledges I did not trust.
